item.title: Re: SCP Greenlight Idea
item.content:encoded:
This reminds me a lot of SCP-1459 but with less charm to it and more of a focus on…just, cruelty? Idk I don't hugely vibe with the core concept as presented but at the same time, this could be interesting if you y'know, did something with it? Like, a SCP article is a short story: you've got the stuff setting up what the anomaly is but what I really want to know is 'what do you do with the anomaly': how do the Foundation interact with this? What challenges does it raise for them? How do the company that made it and the circus known for animal cruelty tie in here? How are you showing the full horror of this thing instead of just leaving it all implied by the description?

item.title: Re: House of Memories
item.content:encoded:
+ Open for critique
- Behold!

This idea feels like you started with the house memory concept then forced a narrative around it that doesn't really make sense with it. These are pulling in different directions. The potential horror of the house drawing people in with visions of past events is masked and watered down by this extra story surrounding the child and their grandmother. Depending on the way you decide to go (honestly either way works, just not in the same article) you should flip your focus.

The core anomaly with a creature drawing people in, it being in the mountains, so on feels like SCP-3333 without the intrigue. While this is nitpicky, it feels very odd that this child, an amateur thaumaturge, would be able to curse a house with shapeshifters, a lure ability, and manage to corrupt themselves. While the last point makes sense, it feels like they succeeded if their mission was to curse a house.

What exactly are the d-class mission going to reveal in this article? As of right now, it feels tacked on as a way of adding length. Is the stinger going to be found here? I suppose yes but your narrative leads me to believe that everything about this family will be revealed before this happens. Also, what would the stinger be?

As of right now, I do not feel confident enough to greenlight this idea.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: House of Memories

While this has somewhat interesting ideas in how it handles 4000 lore and Santa Claus, I feel it fails to explore them in sufficient depth for it to be a satisfying article. -1


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-5925

+1

At first when I got that it was the Trolley Problem I thought it would be just a cheap ethical experiment and probably downvote. But in the end it is a very interesting logical exercise using the Problem just as a device. Indeed, for me it highlights just how obtuse is the Trolley Problem and the two extreme takes on ethics it clashes.

For me the convoluted procedure justifies itself on the basis of reliability. Six can't say what happens if the dog is killed or if they kills themself. There is a need to keep things going if Six dies first. Also Six cannot guarantee their own follow-up of procedure if put under constant direct moral stress.

Deontology focus on action doesn't mean that it affords complete inaction, either. The Trolley problem puts 1 life against 5 because even for a deontologist it would be immoral to kill through inaction if the saving action had no moral consequence. More importantly, what's at stake isn't arguing how deontology works, but how the anomaly will interpret it, and then a less complex procedure would carry the risk of a breach.

item.title: Seeking greenlight for SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: An archive of written material that has been lost to the rest of the world. Deleted files, burned documents, things like that. Some of this information would be very dangerous if it got out. The archive and its contents are usually imperceptible, but Foundation mnestics allow it and the materials therin to be seen and remembered. However, mnestic drugs are not strong enough to perceive its guardian, who does not want intruders in its archive.

Central Narrative: Researchers initially appear to have only recently discovered the skip and are making plans to have it explored and studied further. Then someone realizes that they have documentation from prior testing and exploration that no one remembers ordering. They have apparently sent multiple D-Class and MTF agents into the skip, but none of them have come out. Also, no other documentation of the existence of said personnell exists outside of DEEPWELL archives. One agent emerges from the skip physically unharmed, but showing symptoms of psychological trauma. The agent can't remember what may have caused said trauma or why they are the only member of their task force on record. The Foundation can tell something is up and suspends testing. This is not the first time this sequence has repeated, perhaps end the article with the start of a new cycle of testing and forgetting.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I really enjoy articles you have to think about to understand. I want to not actually state that there is a monster in the archive, rather I'd like to let readers figure that out on their own in a way that both makes them feel clever and accomplished and provides fridge horror type creep factor.

Additional Notes: I'm going to need help with the structure of the article if this ends up being something that interests people. I'll also need some help making the Foundation not look incompetent while preserving the mystery aspect. This needs to be something that seems reasonable for the Foundation to have misinterpreted.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Seeking greenlight for SCP

No O5 voted, this is a ruse. And nothing happens to the person affected except a complete belief that they are 100% objectively bad.

Dr. Six is, indeed, affected all the time, but manages this. The problem is that if this thing gets out of control it won't be likely that enough personnel will stay able to fulfil their duties to the Foundation.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] SCP Concept Critique
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard containment procedures and description, with background on its discovery. Interview and test logs showing how its anomalous effects were deduced, as well as further experimentation.

Elevator Pitch: A mattress/mattresses that induces vivid dreams in those who sleep in it. Upon waking up, their memories are retroactively altered to include, and frequently overridden with the contents of their dreams (e.g. a man who dreams of fishing may believe he had been a fisherman his whole life; a person who dreams of a deceased loved one believes they are still alive).

Central Narrative: A hospital gains Foundation attention after an outbreak of manic patients. Investigation leads to the discovery of the SCP. The affected patients are taken into Foundation custody to be examined so as to further understand the nature of the SCP.

The possibility of the SCP being used to treat treatment-resistant conditions is explored, leading to extensive testing. Humorous and dramatic attempts follow due to the SCP's unreliable nature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a memory-altering SCP that relies on the user's dreams to fabricate memories.

Additional Notes: I'm open to suggestions or developments to the concept and narrative.

Forum thread: [Seeking Greenlight] SCP Concept Critique

item.title: Re: Ms. G. Lass
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Angryman22. Let’s take a look at your concept.

It starts off promising, but I’m struggling to connect the various anomalous together. For example, what does a survivor of a glass factory explosion have to do with “a strong hatred for transparent objects”? Furthermore, why is it that when they’re “exposed to even a very small amount of oxygen, they will engulf in flames reaching a temperature of 4000K”?

You appear to be adding these anomalous properties without consideration for purpose or reason. At best, this sounds like a possible body horror scip if you manage to delve deeper into the psychology of the humanoid. Tell us more about who Georgine Lass was/is. Why is she behaving the way she is after the explosion? At worst, however, this scip sounds like your typical Peter Parker-gets-bitten-by-a-radioactive-spider-and-becomes-a-superhero sort of story. Even then, you need to flesh out the character’s motivations and goals and tell us why she’s behaving as such.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: THE BOOK BETWEEN LIFE AND DEATH
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via Pm
Interesting SCP you've got there
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So while this idea has some potential, there are a LOT of things you need to fix before I (and many other concept reviewers) will consider giving you a greenlight.

  • Elevator pitch: Don't tell me your idea isn't special. You're trying to sell me on the idea, so you need to be confident about it. Writing "um this book isn't special" is an immediate turn off. Try and find something unique. It doesn't have to be revolutionary or groundbreaking: just unique and intriguing enough to get someone to read through it.
  • Central Narrative: I'm sorry, but I barely understand the story you're going for. Where did the entity come from? Why did the serpent's hand ally with the Foundation? What brought SCP-1000 into the situation? You need to make your idea more concise. It's barely half baked right now: mising al the details that a successful article has. You honestly need to work on your idea before moving forward.
  • Hook: You need more than just a pair of O5s to get your story to appear interesting. Tel me why I should read your article rather than another article. Also, where did Merlin come from?
  • Additional Notes: This idea needs to go back in the oven IT's lacking the crucial components and skill necessary for creating a coherent and compelling piece. This idea is salvageable, but you need to really work on your writing skills. Apologies if anything here sounded rude, as that was not my intent.

item.title: "The Homeless Man" - SCP Idea - GL
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

A humanoid figure looking like a starving man.
Any human who goes near it that laughs gets attacked, bitten/ripped, and peeled by the SCP.
He's locked in a simple windowless room.

Central Narrative:

Starts off in urban Florida 2019, where the SCP was presumed to be a homeless man living on the street.
It was there for 2 years, not doing anything until it was caught trying to peel (with teeth) a local teen's skin off.
Video footage was captured (eventually uploaded online), and the SCP quickly-crawled away with the body.

+ show block
– hide block

Foundation field agents were warned and investigated after widespread local fear of SCP-XXXX online.
MTF Search-Teams found SCP-XXXX by an urban lake.
SCP's didn't eat, breathe, talk or scream, and walked on all fours similar to a spider.
It was captured by MTF. (Audio Attached)

Foundation put coverup stories, making a fake background, court charges, and sentencing.
Foundation took a list of items where SCP was recorded: Printed photos of people of ranging ages and an old coat SCP wore made of skin parts of different animals.

Research on the photos (attached) revealed the people were that of now-dead people.
People were that of children, adults, prison inmates, and one of the leading researchers of the Foundation.
Connections between lists of people could not be found by staff, but details of who they are, are given.
Hidden letters on the photos revealed words "fam", "peel", "ric", "sorrow", "controlling", "it's gone", and "give it back".
A note was found in the coat that stated "Life is given to those with lemons, a bad one is given to those with oranges".

D-class was used to experiment on the SCP, audio recordings, and experiment chart was attached.
SCP-XXXX didn't react or attack until the third experiment, where the D-Class chuckled nervously.
More experiments occurred until Foundation found out SCP-XXXX only reacts to D-class laughing at certain distances.

SCP-XXXX was watched over after every kill, in which he was seen to make shapes with the pieces of skin.
Foundation gave SCP-XXXX crayons and paper, but it only used skin to make shapes.
Recreated drawings were made (and attached), with the most identifiable ones as an orange, a house, a frowning face, and a knife.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Creepiness is from lack of info on the lore.

Additional Notes:

item.title: Re: What is the **out** of universe reason for discontinuing MTF Omega 7 Pandoras Box?
item.content:encoded:
From what I've read, it was a good idea that was taken out of hand. We're trying to give it another shot with Alpha-9, but the key is, we need to stop thinking X-Men and more Suicide Squad. When I first got here and found out about these MTFs, my thinking was that it is very hard to contain all these things and if some are useful, use them, and if some are people who may be cooperative, make them earn their keep. The idea should be SCPs are being put to work because it's expensive to house and feed them so the least they can do is help when we need them, assuming they will help at all. But it turns into a Mary-Sue fest because people want to make superheroes from anomalies instead of considering SCPs as horrors first and a last resort to solve other problems when nothing else works. Omega-7 went off the rails and the authors put the rabid beast down, and if we are going to give it a second shot, make sure the writers know the idea is anomalies that got caught and are out on work release.

Forum thread: What is the **out** of universe reason for discontinuing MTF Omega 7 Pandoras Box?

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hey. EponymousRex. Occasionally go by SteelGriffin or Griff sometimes. Long time reader, first time proper official poster. Heh, fiddled around with discussion the old IRC a fair number of years ago. Wanted to write someone/something as a comical doom magnet. Some poor dude attracting suffering enough to make him hate his pitiful existence, but never enough to end it. As if that hasn't been done to death, and honestly I'm surprised I remember it. Oh well.

I might try to do something more than read and so on, but probably not for awhile. Not until I'm over my anxiety and general cowardice.

I always found the Idea beyond the SCP setting, and the general mechanics of it as a collectively written universe to be fascinating. A massive cooperative writing project that has produced something so wonderful and thought provoking, not to mention Fun. So not only am I here for the stories, I'm here to watch the community, and I'm kicking myself for not deciding to become involved sooner.

Anyway to answer the question prompt. Despite my previous noting on my own anxieties, that rarely keeps me up that much. It's more just… My mind gets going on some idea, some story, some THING I want to write, create, etc. Though I do worry. About Family, about the future, all that crap. You know how it is.

item.title: Twas the night before Christmas, and inside the shed, was a pile of upvotes, all stacked on a sled
item.content:encoded:
The odd phrases in the parentheses adds the essential layer of surrealism to this, which is why I loved seeing this. I was already going to upvote when I was done reading, but the "Naught but dust" made me scroll up and give a +1. Normally, perspective tales on a hostile anomaly have a strangely-edgy atmosphere that I don't usually care for, but this one adds a well-crafted, alien-like mindset to the creature, and also does it well.

Edit: Also, throwing in "Christmas" as a catch-all word for the creature was extremely unsettling, and really gave the tale atmosphere.

item.title: Re: My first SCP article
item.content:encoded:
No, Satan's appearance wasn't mentioned in the Bible (I read the whole thing, I know) that's why I attributed it to Scapegoats, it's the only mention of goats and sin so I connected the dots.

The goats die at the end of the ritual? Since when has death stopped an SCP? One word: Undead. The weight of the sins won't let their souls rest, so even though they died, they rise again, that's why they have to be contained, the GOC tried killing them but it totally did not work at all.

Actually, the mountain thing is better, now I have a location where they can be contained, much more important than an angel.

Again, sorry if it came off as anti-semitic, "sins of the nation of Israel" came from how it was worded in the Bible. I just wanted to give an origin to the demon goat archetype that made sense to me. But whatever, I have other ideas, either we work out the kinks or I drop it to the bottom of the list and pick a different one. I just wanted to see what would get attention. But if you hate it, that's not the attention I want.

Now that I know what you don't like, was there one on my list you did like and would rather I focus on instead?

item.title: Re: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
That said, does the story itself at least sound compelling?

Personally I'm lukewarm on it. The general gist seems to just be "human is stuck in a different world and at the whim of a distressed deity like figure, eventually escapes". I myself am uncertain what the reader is supposed to take away from the story besides "it sucks to be the characters in this story". There's a lot of specific details about what these individuals end up doing, but the guy just escaping at the end doesn't feel super meaningful or impactful for me. I would probably want to see the guy convince the deity to let him go or to help him find a way to leave. Maybe he leaves something in that world and promises to return. Maybe he takes something with him in exchange. Something more than just "guy conveniently manages to get out of there, the end".

item.title: Re: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Or, obvious solution. Periods of intermittent rainfall. It IS an oceanic world, after all, and that could be enough to give him fresh water. Would that work to solve the water problem? And in the meantime, maintaining a diverse undersea ecosystem, while leaning away from the manufactured "paradise" aspects of the world. Trade and communication, yes, but less emphasis on the world being "perfect."

Steering away from the mechanics for a moment, what I want to focus on in this story is more the power dynamic that can arise from three different species trapped on a world where one of them has a distinct advantage, one is relatively free to travel - being a winged creature - and one is borderline helpless. I wanted to explore the psychology of the creatures by putting the human at a distinct disadvantage in this scenario, adding to the horror of the situation.

That being said, I need some days to let the psychology run its course. I plan to have a cetacean who's initially friendly and caring, but who desperately misses her pod, and uses the human to compensate for company. They'd travel together for some days, with the cetacean realizing that the scientist is dependent on her to provide food, leading to (in her mind) a benevolent power imbalance and letting her fill the void that came from being separated from her pod.

+ show block
– hide block

This gets complicated when a flying arachnid appears, and the scientist interacts with it as well, despite some initial trepidation. I intend for the cetacean to become jealous and possessive, seeing the human as "hers" and resenting that the power imbalance with the arachnid isn't as pronounced, as it can at least leave and fly away from her for a while, even if it's still dependent on food for her - it's a small amount of freedom, but enough to irk the cetacean and drive her towards madness.

This would come to a head when the cetacean would encourage the insect to "pull its own weight," concocting a scheme whereby she drains its strength while encouraging it to take on scouting duties while she stays with "her" human. The insect gets weaker as a result, and eventually crashes into the ocean, where it's left (barely) ambiguous as to whether the cetacean kills it while retrieving it, leaving her alone with "her" human.

From that point on, the human is the utter captive of the cetacean, and she starts treating him poorly - giving him half-chewed food that she "deigns" to allow him to have, keeping him up and not allowing him to sleep, and psychologically torturing him by emphasizing that he can live or die at her whim. He only manages to escape when he finds one of the few tiny islands on the world, giving him a brief reprieve, though now he's under siege from the cetacean. He manages to escape when one of the teleportation orbs filled with mist washes up on shore, and he mixes it with water from his own ocean, allowing him to teleport home, leaving the cetacean the sole, lonely inhabitant of a former, now-empty paradise.
